shouldFix.title: The three prohibitions in policy.hostMustNot — the contract's most contested law — have no retained negative class, while six classes exist for other laws
shouldFix.finding: policy.hostMustNot states three prohibitions in the artifact's own voice: the host must not mint a fail/warn verdict, must not invent a D9 code, and must not treat policyOutcome as HostTermination. Mapped from the artifact's own bytes, none of NT-1 through NT-6 exercises any of them. NT-1 tests pack identity, NT-2 declarative-only, NT-3 the missing rung, NT-4 component findings, NT-5 SARIF and NT-6 sealed-Run relabelling. This is the one law where the corpus has already had to correct itself: the original architecture-completion consensus round withdrew the phrase 'host fail/warn threshold' precisely because it relocated policy out of the pure core, and OBL-4 exists to state the corrected law. A contract that fixes a law after it was got wrong once, volunteers a six-class test set for its other laws, and then leaves that law unexercised has under-specified its own retained evidence at the point of greatest risk. The parallel is exact to the sibling chain: provider-only-output-contract.v2 was returned for naming prohibitions with no retained class, and its v3 added NT-6 and NT-7 to close them.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: DR-131's acceptance cell requires a contract that freezes the named laws; unlike DR-133's cell it does not require retained negative tests, so the classes are volunteered rather than owed. The law itself is stated correctly and the three prohibitions are unambiguous. The gap is coverage of the artifact's own stated prohibitions, not a failure to answer the cell.
shouldFix.repair: Add one or two classes in the existing idiom. A host-mints-verdict class: input is a host path that derives fail or warn other than from the core's policyOutcome; pass is refusal, with the verdict taken only from CoreCompletion. A host-mints-D9-or-termination class: input is a host path that mints a D9 class, exit number or HostTermination from the analyze result rather than mapping an existing v1.14 class after finalization; pass is refusal, with the mapping remaining DR-007 / v1.14 host-owned. Both are constructible against the same host surfaces NT-3 and NT-6 already assume.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, with 2 advisories. Seventeen attacks run, two landed, neither at blocker grade. Custody is intact: subject ba2a0a68 at 0444 unmoved and valid JSON, HEAD never left f5094f0, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree. This is the strongest first version in the three contract chains for this goal — the DR-133 and DR-117 contracts each carried two blockers at v1 and this one carries none. Every attack in the prompt's list is refuted against measured bytes: the row quote is exact on all three strings, the nine obligations reconstruct the acceptance cell with nothing unassigned including the trailing DR-123 exclusion, no §7.1 recipe or D9 code is invented, the DR-123 generics are expressly not re-owned, and the D-002 SARIF reconciliation is complete and accurate at every clause — I checked D-002's adopted text, the DR-006 ride and its symmetry clause, D-077's Decision and G17's inapplicability against their own bytes rather than file 12's summary, since file 12 has no authority. Both cited owner-recording commits match file 08's DR-006 and DR-007 cells, and both sibling contract digests reproduce live. What blocks is coverage of the contract's own most contested law. policy.hostMustNot names three prohibitions — the host must not mint a fail/warn verdict, must not invent a D9 code, must not treat policyOutcome as HostTermination — and none of the six volunteered classes exercises any of them. That law is the one the corpus already had to correct once: the original consensus round withdrew 'host fail/warn threshold' precisely because it relocated policy out of the pure core, and OBL-4 exists to state the corrected version. The sibling chain closed the identical gap when provider-only-output-contract.v3 added NT-6 and NT-7. I disclose that I was the reviewer who forced the original correction, so the finding is about testing that law rather than restating it. The advisories are that joins.d078.citedLaw drops 'and DR-G21 goldens' from D-078's clause — harmless here since containment goldens are not this row's subject, but a citedLaw field invites a complete quotation — and, venued to the recording entry rather than the artifact, that DR-131's cell carries the same 'no contract exists' clause DR-133 did, so whichever entry records this contract should carry D-136's Decision 6 form and D-137 turn 2's D-056-eligibility statement.
